claims.quote: CLN2 disease is an inherited metabolic storage disorder caused by the deficiency of the lysosomal enzyme tripeptidyl peptidase 1 (TPP1).
The disease affects mainly the brain and the retina and is characterized by progressive dysfunction of the central nervous system, leading to dementia, epilepsy, loss of motor function and blindness.

claims.subject_mention: enzyme delivery through the cerebrospinal fluid
claims.quote: Enzyme delivery through the cerebrospinal fluid led to wide distribution of enzyme activity in the brain and to attenuated neuropathology and disease progression in a TPP1-deficient mouse model as well as in a natural TPP1-deficient dog model.

Safety of the intrathecal delivery, pharmacokinetics, and tissue distribution of the administered enzyme studied in non-human primates were encouraging, and a phase I/II clinical trial for intraventricular ERT in CLN2 patients is ongoing.

claims.subject_mention: intracerebral injection of viral vectors containing CLN2 gene
claims.quote: In a CLN2 mouse model, this procedure resulted in cerebral enzyme expression, reduced brain pathology and increased survival.
A small number of patients have been treated the same way using an AAV2-vector for gene transfer to the brain.
